question: Can a direct-grid Xe2 DPAS kernel reproduce the natural-M1/source-M4 eight-way K reduction exactly, without the oneDNN catalog geometry's M128 scheduling penalty?

trigger.r140: The source-M32 fixed-K server was row invariant but matched only 8/12 frozen c1 token arrays, proving that row invariance alone is insufficient when anchored to the wrong arithmetic class.
trigger.r141: The natural-M1/source-M4 arithmetic class was reproduced exactly by all valid oneDNN wgK8 candidates, but the fastest candidate modeled 1.349335x natural latency at M128, failing the 1.03x decode gate.
trigger.required_mechanism: Retain an eight-way, 64-K-position local reduction while replacing general oneDNN scheduling with an exact dense output-tile grid.

provenance.source_tree_rule: Use a new clean clone and build root. Do not build from or modify the dirty R127 source tree.

frozen_kernel.launch: One direct-grid workgroup per ceil(M/16) by ceil(N/64) output tile; no persistent scheduler, rows tensor, global atomic queue, or per-call scratch allocation.
frozen_kernel.mma: XE_DPAS_TT<8,float,half_t> with WGTile [16,64,512] and SGLayout shape [1,4,8], stride [32,8,1].
frozen_kernel.k_partition: The eight K subgroups each accumulate one 64-position contiguous slice of every 512-position macro-tile. Production K values 3072, 5120, and 8704 are all divisible by 512.
frozen_kernel.scales: For subgroup k_sg, use block scale floor((macro_k*512 + k_sg*64)/128); the two adjacent 64-position subgroups therefore share one 128-wide block scale.
frozen_kernel.reduction: Each subgroup writes its FP32 C fragment to a 32-KiB workgroup-local buffer. After a release/acquire workgroup barrier, only k_sg=0 reads the eight corresponding fragments, reduces them in the frozen candidate order, and writes FP16 output.
frozen_kernel.output_layout: Production NT logical weights: input tensor [1,K,N], interpreted as B [N,K], with FP32 scales [1,K/128,N/128].
frozen_kernel.allowed_build_narrowing: Instantiate only FP16 activation, E4M3 weight, FP32 BLOCK_FP8 scale, no-bias, one-expert dense diagnostic dispatch. Build narrowing may not alter kernel semantics.

screen.identity_reference: R141 forced source-M4 output, after directly reconfirming its row 0 equals natural M1 on each shape.
screen.identity: Every full output at every M must be bitwise equal to the source-M4 reference; repeat M128, seeded M128 permutation, and 168-to-200 padding must also be exact.
screen.timing: Ten warmups, five samples of 100 synchronized calls at M2, M64, M128, M168, and M256, compared with natural oneDNN in the same process protocol.
screen.stability: No candidate timed-sample max/min ratio may exceed 1.15.

gates.compile: The frozen kernel must build without workgroup-size, local-memory-size, spill, or registration failure.
gates.arithmetic_discovery: Test reduction orders in the listed order. Stop at the first order exact on both shapes and all M values; do not tune geometry or invent a fourth order in this campaign.
gates.on_no_exact_order: Close the guessed-reduction prototype without latency expansion and instrument the oneDNN JIT reduction/store path before another kernel attempt.
gates.decode_model: The exact candidate must model <=1.15x natural on the two screened shapes at each of M2, M64, and M128 before expansion. The relaxed 1.15 diagnostic gate is only for deciding whether the mechanism deserves all-six-shape work; endpoint promotion still requires the prior <=1.03 weighted decode budget and >=54 tok/s.
gates.prefill: M168 and M256 must each be <=2.0x natural.
gates.on_pass: Expand the identical arithmetic and layout to all six production shapes, model the frozen per-layer call mix, and only then preregister a server image and endpoint run.
gates.on_failure: Preserve the result and do not launch a server or begin collective optimization.

abort_conditions: any current-boot Xe fault, CAT error, reset, coredump, device loss, timeout, or hung stage visible to the available health interfaces
either B70 is not normal before or after a device case
any unregistered reduction order, geometry change, candidate substitution, or server launch
